subject: Architecture
title: The Home Insurance Building: First Skyscraper
description: A quick, practical guide to The Home Insurance Building: First Skyscraper.

hook.text: The world's first skyscraper was only ten stories tall — but it changed cities forever.

buildup.text: In 1885, Chicago engineer William Le Baron Jenney used a steel skeleton instead of thick stone walls.

discovery.text: Steel frames carry the weight. Walls become thin curtains — windows could finally be large.

twist.text: Jenney got the idea watching his wife place a heavy book on a wire birdcage that didn't collapse.

climax.text: Every skyscraper on Earth uses this principle: the frame holds everything, walls just keep weather out.

punchline.text: A birdcage and a book invented the modern skyline.

quiz.question: What innovation made the first skyscraper possible?
options: Reinforced concrete floors poured on site
A steel skeleton frame instead of load-bearing walls
Hydraulic elevators powered by steam engines
